The next strategy created after the rebalance reuses the dead pool. Its submit() raises queue.ShutDown, which is caught in SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit, and the offset is then marked complete. Messages are dropped without processing and their offsets get committed. The offset tracker also keeps stale state across strategies.

Unbounded queues give no backpressure
queue.Queue() is unbounded and submit never blocks, contrary to the docstring's backpressure claim; memory grows if processing is slower than consumption.

Commit loop does not handle rebalance and shares state across partitions
The queue pool and offset tracker are owned by the factory and shared across strategy instances created on each rebalance; old strategy close() shuts down the shared pool, and the factory's queue_pool is then dead for the new strategy. Also the commit loop commits after a final wait without a final flush on close, and tracker state for revoked partitions persists.

Offsets completed even when processing fails
The finally block marks the offset complete even when result_processor raised, so failed messages get committed and are lost. A `break` on ShutDown also completes an unprocessed offset, allowing commit of unprocessed work.
